A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MISBOT study. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original detector experiments, annotation-quality evaluations, modality ablations, and analyses of bot participation, content similarity, sentiments, and stances.

after.justification: v3 retains the original detector experiments, annotation evaluations, ablations, and analyses of misinformation and social bots.

M1.justification: The entity-based collection procedure, calibrated expert ensemble, multimodal misinformation detector, and clustering algorithm remain unchanged. The expanded MLP descriptions in Section 2.4 were already documented in v2 Appendix A.11.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Chinese Weibo corpus, including 11,393 misinformation posts and 16,416 real-information posts, and the same account data and analysis tasks. The EWECT and STANCE datasets used for sentiment and stance classifiers are also retained.

E2.justification: Table 7 retains the same eleven bot-detection experts and aggregate comparison variants. Tables 2 and 6 retain the same misinformation detector variants. Newly cited research is not added to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The 8:1:1 account split, topic-separated ten-fold detector evaluation, hyperparameters, ROUGE-L sampling, and hourly sentiment analysis remain unchanged. Specifying reposts, comments, and likes in the echo-chamber discussion clarifies participation already defined in v2 Section 2.1.

E4.justification: The modality ablations and image, topic-similarity, sentiment, stance, correlation, and bot-behavior analyses are retained. The bot-comment analysis in v2 Appendix C.10 and Figure 18 is incorporated into v3 Section 4 and Figure 9 rather than replaced by a new analysis.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 6 retain means and standard deviations from ten-fold cross-validation and paired t-tests with the same 0.0005 threshold. Fleiss’ Kappa and Cohen’s Kappa reporting is unchanged; moving the existing agreement result into the annotation discussion adds no statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Section 4 newly characterizes cluster sizes as long-tailed, without supplying a corresponding quantitative distribution analysis. Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including Table 2’s 95.2% accuracy and 92.3% F1 and the bot-comment category counts redisplayed in v3 Figure 9.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulas for data structures, temperature scaling, detector components, clustering, pairwise similarity, and sentiment variation are unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 removes the abstract’s claim to be the first study exploring social bots and misinformation on Sina Weibo. The dataset contribution and the three central findings about participation, echo chambers, and public opinion remain.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 newly emphasizes subjective bot annotation and explains using guidelines without a strict definition. Section 2.3 additionally claims that Section 3 quantitatively establishes source truthfulness, although its checks concern separability and bot annotations. The existing graph-coverage, recall, and platform limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the GitHub repository pointer with a project-homepage link. Its Ethics Statement narrows the promised controlled access from data and model checkpoints to annotator checkpoints. Implementation settings and pretrained-model references remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish actual changes in online availability.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Cresci (2020), Wang et al. (2018), and Himelein-Wachowiak et al. (2021), explicitly acknowledging earlier bot–misinformation research. Section 5 adds several detection papers from 2024–2025. These are bounded literature updates within the existing positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of Sections 1–4 undergo paragraph-level rewriting, with expanded explanations and appendix pointers integrated into the narrative. Appendix A.5–A.7 is reordered, Appendix C.10 is absorbed into Section 4, and affiliations and acknowledgements are expanded.

P2.justification: v2 Figure 18 moves into the main text as v3 Figure 9 and changes from stacked bars to separate sentiment and stance category bars. Other plots receive color, label, and aspect-ratio adjustments, and Table 1 relocates. The overall figure and table content is retained.

improvement.justification: The more cautious novelty claim, explicit annotation-subjectivity qualification, clearer explanations, and more accessible bot-comment figure modestly improve the paper. Methods and quantitative evidence remain stable. These gains are partly offset by the added claim that Section 3 proves source truthfulness, which its reported checks do not establish.
